title: Madagascar — Down the RN7 Between Rain and Sandstone
subtitle: Highland rice terraces, an eastern rainforest, granite and sandstone canyons, and the dry south-west in the wet season
summary: A 14-day driver-guided road trip down the RN7 from Antananarivo to Toliara, built around the parts of Madagascar that can be visited in the wet season, with the Tsingy and Avenue of the Baobabs left out.
introduction: This route follows the RN7 south from Antananarivo through Antsirabe and Ambositra, drops into the Ranomafana rainforest for two days, and crosses the granite country of Ambalavao to the sandstone canyons of Isalo. It ends in the spiny forest of the dry south-west before a flight back to the capital. It is a driver-guided journey with a camping night at Isalo, markets, woodcarving workshops and lemur walks. February and March are the wet and cyclone months, so the plan leaves one flexible day, avoids the Tsingy de Bemaraha and the east coast, and drives only in daylight.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is desert with self-drive on empty tracks; this is a hired driver-guide on a single national highway, with rainforest, lemurs and highland rice-terrace villages, and rain rather than heat as the main weather risk.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Standard Madagascar tours go in the dry season and include the Tsingy and the Avenue of the Baobabs. This trip is built for the wet season, with community-run reserves, handmade paper and woodcarving workshops, and a night camping at Isalo.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination in the portfolio has endemic lemurs on granite boulders and in rainforest within one week, but it is also the one where weather and cyclone risk most affect the plan, and where the best-known sites (Tsingy, baobabs) are not visitable in the window.

duration.note: Day 1 is the overnight flight from Paris; day 13 is the domestic flight and night flight home, arriving day 14.

recommendedTravelWindow.window: Late March 2027, ideally the last two weeks
recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Rain and cyclone risk fall from February to March, and April is the shoulder month. March is the last wet month with fewer cyclones and more sunny days, while February is often the month with the highest cyclone risk. Flights are also slightly cheaper in March.

februarySuitability.summary: Peak of the wet and cyclone season. Heavy daily rain on the highlands and rainforest, flooded or damaged roads possible, tropical storms; Isalo and the south-west are drier but still hot and stormy.

marchSuitability.summary: Still wet, but cyclone risk falls and sunny spells become more frequent. The RN7 is normally passable, though delays and landslides are possible. The Tsingy and Andringitra high trekking remain out of scope.

climate.regionNote: Figures are approximate climate norms for the highland plateau at about 1,300 m (Antananarivo, Antsirabe), the eastern rainforest at Ranomafana, and the dry south-west at Toliara. They are not from an official meteorological page I fetched and are planning estimates.

february.rainfall: Highlands and Ranomafana: very wet, roughly 250-400 mm; Isalo: wet, roughly 150-200 mm; Toliara: about 60-90 mm. Approximate norms.
february.humidity: High on the plateau and rainforest; lower in Toliara
february.notes: February is often the month with the highest tropical cyclone risk (Intrepid). Many secondary roads impassable except by 4x4 (FCDO).

march.rainfall: Highlands and Ranomafana: wet, roughly 200-350 mm; Isalo: roughly 100-150 mm; Toliara: about 40-70 mm. Approximate norms.
march.notes: March is described as the last off-season month with fewer cyclones and more sunny days (Intrepid).

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: No snow. Rain closes or degrades trails. Andringitra's Pic Boby trek is a multi-day wet-season undertaking and could not be verified as open, so it is not in the plan. The Tsingy de Bemaraha is generally closed in the wet season (SafariBookings: opens about April/May to November), so it is excluded.
climate.seaConditions: Warm Indian Ocean water (about 28 degrees) on the Toliara coast; the south-west is the driest coast but cyclone swell can reach it.
climate.airQuality: Smoke from burning on the plateau is a dry-season issue; not relevant in the wet season.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Lemurs are active year round; chameleons and frogs are more visible in the wet season; many lemur species give birth around the start of the rains. Birdlife is rich.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Martyrs' Day
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Public holiday; some offices closed. Easter 2027 falls on 28 March, so Easter week may affect domestic demand.

climate.ramadan2027: Not relevant: Madagascar is mainly Christian and traditional-religion; Ramadan has little effect except in a few Muslim communities in the north-west, which this route does not visit.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Not relevant: Lunar New Year has no effect in Madagascar.
climate.tourismDemand: Low; February and March are the low season, so lodges are quiet and prices can be negotiated.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Fare statistics show March as the cheapest month, with February slightly higher; summer peaks well above.

geography.summary: The central plateau, a sandstone massif, the rainforest escarpment and the semi-arid south-west.
geography.distinctive: Four climate and ecological zones in 1,500 km of road, almost all of their species found nowhere else.

travelStyle.summary: Driver-guide for the RN7, on-foot walks inside parks, one camping night.

transport.summary: A private driver-guide with a 4x4 or minibus covers the RN7 and a single domestic flight returns from Toliara.

modes.description: Standard for the RN7; booked through a local operator. Daytime driving only.
Madagascar Airlines (Tsaradia); schedules and reliability should be checked.
For short trips in Antsirabe and Toliara.

transport.carRental: Self-drive rental exists (for example Roadtrip Africa) but the RN7 involves potholes, trucks and robbery risk at night; a local driver-guide is recommended.

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-drive is possible but not recommended; roads are poor and night driving is advised against.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: An IDP and a home licence are normally needed for self-drive; confirm with the rental company.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences, but none is needed with a driver-guide.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Nobody rides a motorcycle or scooter without the required licence; motorbike taxis are discouraged by CDC.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Hire a driver-guide, drive only in daylight, and keep a flexible day.

accommodation.summary: Mid-range hotels and ecolodges with one camping night.

camping.summary: Camping is possible at authorised sites in Isalo, subject to weather; wild camping is not advised given the banditry risk in the south.

physicalDifficulty.label: demanding
physicalDifficulty.summary: Daily walks of 3-6 h on wet trails, heat in the south, and several 4-6 h days in a vehicle.

itinerary.summary: Fly in, spend two days on the highlands, two in the Ranomafana rainforest, then go south to Ambalavao, Isalo and Toliara and fly back to Antananarivo for the night flight home.

stops.description: UNESCO-listed Atsinanana rainforest on steep eastern escarpment, home to golden bamboo lemur, greater bamboo lemur and Milne-Edwards's sifaka. The wettest stop on the route.

Meet the community-run tourism groups

scenarioNotes.economical: Cheapest fares, simple guesthouses, 50 euro driver-guide day and a 10 euro entry fee; weather risk is unchanged.

security.summary: No official source I could read puts any region on the route under advice against travel, but the advice is mixed: UK FCDO warns of dahalo attacks and convoy robberies on the RN7 south of Ihosy, the Netherlands is yellow, the US reported Level 2 (page not readable) and France reports calm. A post-uprising transitional government since October 2025, the cyclone and wet season, and the Ebola entry restrictions leave the route conditional.
security.assessedRoute: Antananarivo, Antsirabe, Ambositra, Ranomafana, Fianarantsoa, Ambalavao, Isalo (Ranohira), Toliara, Ifaty. Outside the route: Tsingy de Bemaraha and the west coast (RN35, Besalampy-Morombe), Fort Dauphin and Anosy, Betroka, Nosy Be and the north, the east coast.

advisories.level: No region under advice against travel; regional cautions for the south and west
advisories.regionsAffected: South (Ihosy, Toliara, Fort Dauphin, Ilakaka, RN7 convoys), west highway robberies
advisories.routeImpact: RN7 south of Ambalavao is named: use a recognised operator, daytime only.

advisories.level: Public order calm for several months; zone map not retrieved; alerts on Ebola, El Nino and measles
advisories.routeImpact: Detailed zones could not be read, so the colour of the route is unverified.

advisories.regionsAffected: Central-west interior toward Bemaraha, Anosy and Betroka

advisories.level: Level 2, reported (page not readable; rechecking needed)
advisories.routeImpact: Not confirmed from the live page.

conflictRisk.note: No armed conflict, but the October 2025 change of power and Russian Africa Corps presence create political uncertainty; anniversaries and demonstrations may bring road closures.

terrorismRisk.note: No terrorism concern is highlighted by the advisories read.

kidnappingRisk.note: Dahalo cattle raiders and armed highway robbers operate in the south and west; attacks on convoys on the RN7 are recorded by the FCDO.

regionalRestrictions: FCDO names dahalo attacks near Ilakaka and Isalo and between Ihosy, Toliara and Fort Dauphin
FCDO advises a recognised tour operator in the south and no night driving
The Tsingy de Bemaraha route (RN35, Besalampy-Morombe) is excluded and also closed in the wet season
Foreign nationals arriving from or via DR Congo are barred (Ebola); Kenya and Nigeria transits need a health undertaking
ordinaryRisks: Pickpocketing and muggings in Antananarivo and at isolated beaches near Toliara
security.medicalAccess: Basic. Antananarivo hospitals manage routine cases; complex surgery may require evacuation to Mauritius, South Africa or Reunion (FCDO).
security.insuranceConsiderations: Travel insurance with medical evacuation is essential; check exclusions for areas under advice and for cyclone cancellation.
security.reassessmentRequired: Recheck all advisories, cyclone bulletins, RN7 conditions and the Ebola entry restrictions before booking and again before departure; confirm the live France and Smartraveller maps, which could not be read.

practicalRequirements.visa: FCDO: stays up to 15 days without a visa with a 10 euro administration fee; 30-day or 60-day tourist visas on arrival. Rules for French passport holders were not separately verified; confirm with the Embassy of Madagascar.
practicalRequirements.entry: Return or onward ticket; Ebola-related restrictions in force in November 2026 for travellers from DR Congo.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 6 months after arrival and 2 blank pages (FCDO).
permits: Park permits bought at the gate in cash in Ariary
practicalRequirements.insurance: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation and cyclone cover.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Mobile data in towns; poor coverage between them.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cash in Ariary is needed at park gates and most lodges; ATMs are limited in smaller towns.
practicalRequirements.medical: CDC recommends malaria prophylaxis outside Antananarivo, hepatitis A, typhoid and rabies advice. Plague is listed; seasonality should be checked with official health advice. Measles and mpox alerts exist.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Diesel is available in towns; the driver-guide handles refuelling.
